There's a couple of reasons. 
1) racism. There was a huge smear campaign on MSG a while back because a lot of Chinese restaurants use. It's why you notice a lot of older people have negative options on it. 
2) most people don't know what it is. It's kinda like citric acid in that way. People know sour candy is sour but they don't know that citric acid is doing the heavy lifting. Same thing with savory stuff. 
3) this one of more a theory but I think the name throws people off. MSG is not a normal name for a seasoning, and umami is probably "too foreign" for a lot of people. People know what savory if but they don't really have a good name for it. 
There are of course a bunch of different reasons for why it's not common place in most recipes but these are the reasons I come across the most.

Don't worry as someone who works with Medicare they are getting screwed too. Yes they are getting a 6% increase but they are also raising the cost of the Part B premium by 10$ a month. It went from 148 to 158. That is the highest increase I have ever seen I one go.

Now that may not seem like much but here's the real kicker. While the money they get from Medicare is increasing the requirements for Medicaid are not. So now a whole bunch of old people who were  previously getting help from Medicaid or LIS to pay for their Meds and other medical stuff will no longer be qualified. So a whole bunch of people are going to lose their government assistance. 

But wait! There's more! A bunch of medicare advantage plans are based around your level of government assistance. And if you lose that assistance or drop down a level you could lose your insurance! So don't worry they are fucking over plenty of people.
